name: Aérospatiale Alouette II / SA315B Lama
summary: A classic French light turbine helicopter with an open-frame tail boom and bubble cockpit; the Lama variant holds high-altitude records.

wings: Three-blade main rotor on a short mast
engines: Single turboshaft exposed on top behind the cabin
Engine and gearbox sit above the cabin, with no cowling on early versions
fuselage: Bubble cockpit with a bare frame of tubes behind the seats
Skids; open lattice structure behind the cabin

tellTales: Bare open tubular tail boom behind a bubble cockpit
Turbine perched above the cabin on a tubular frame

confusedWith.howToTell: The Bell 47 has a two-blade rotor and a stabilizer bar; the Alouette has three blades and a visible turbine on top.
The Hiller has two blades with paddles and a piston engine; the Alouette has three blades and a turbine.
The H125 has an enclosed body and tail boom; the Alouette II has an open lattice behind the cabin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
